title: ICMR Licenses Three Indigenous Biomedical Technologies to Emcure, Biological E
excerpt: India's premier medical research body transfers a novel cervical cancer therapy and two next-generation enteric vaccine technologies to domestic pharmaceutical manufacturers under its Patent Mitra initiative.
body:
• ICMR licensed SHetA2, a first-in-class anti-HPV therapeutic for cervical precancer, to Emcure Pharmaceuticals for commercial development.
  • Biological E received two next-generation enteric vaccine technologies targeting typhoid, paratyphoid, and Shigella infections.
  • The transfers, made under ICMR's Medical Innovations Patent Mitra initiative, aim to accelerate publicly funded research into affordable treatments.
  • SHetA2 was co-developed with the University of Oklahoma's Stephenson Cancer Center through an Indo-US collaboration.

The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) on July 21 licensed three indigenous biomedical technologies to Indian pharmaceutical and vaccine manufacturers, marking the latest effort to translate publicly funded research into commercial healthcare products. The transfers were completed under the Medical Innovations Patent Mitra initiative, ICMR's structured platform for technology commercialisation launched in March 2025.

Emcure Pharmaceuticals Ltd., the Pune-based drugmaker, received a licence for SHetA2, a novel anti-HPV therapeutic candidate developed for Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN), a precancerous condition of the cervix. Hyderabad-headquartered vaccine manufacturer Biological E Ltd. picked up licences for two next-generation vaccine technologies against enteric bacterial infections.

A Targeted Cancer Therapy Born of Indo-US Research

SHetA2 is described as a first-in-class targeted therapeutic that selectively eliminates HPV-induced precancerous and cervical cancer cells while sparing healthy tissue. The compound was jointly developed by Dr. Showket Hussain of ICMR's National Institute of Cancer Prevention and Research (ICMR-NICPR) and Dr. Doris M. Benbrook of the Stephenson Cancer Center at the University of Oklahoma, USA.

"Together, these technologies have the potential to strengthen India's efforts in cancer prevention and infectious disease control while advancing indigenous development of next-generation therapeutics and vaccines."

— ICMR, official statement

Human papillomavirus (HPV) remains a leading cause of cervical cancer globally. According to researchers, SHetA2 could offer women a safer, more affordable, and less invasive treatment option compared to existing interventions for cervical disease.

Next-Generation Vaccines for Enteric Infections

The two vaccine technologies licensed to Biological E were developed by Dr. Santasabuj Das and his team at ICMR's National Institute for Research in Bacterial Infections (ICMR-NIRBI) in Kolkata. The first is a fusion protein construct based on the outer membrane protein of Salmonella typhi, designed as a next-generation typhoid vaccine candidate. The second is a recombinant vaccine formulation targeting Salmonella typhi, Salmonella paratyphi, and Shigella infections, offering broader protection against major enteric bacterial pathogens.

Typhoid and paratyphoid fevers remain endemic in parts of South Asia, while Shigella-linked dysentery continues to affect vulnerable populations, particularly children. The new vaccine technologies could expand the coverage of existing immunisation programmes in India and other developing countries.

Patent Mitra: Building India's Biomedical IP Ecosystem

"ICMR is committed to ensuring that publicly funded research translates into products that improve health outcomes. These technology transfers demonstrate the growing maturity of India's biomedical innovation ecosystem and represent another step towards achieving self-reliance in healthcare innovation."

— Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Director General, ICMR and Secretary, Department of Health Research

The Medical Innovations Patent Mitra initiative was launched on March 8, 2025, during the International Symposium on Health Technology Assessment and developed under the guidance of NITI Aayog in collaboration with the Department of Pharmaceuticals and the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT). In September 2025, ICMR licensed nine technologies under the same programme at India MedTech Expo, resulting in 17 licensing deals. In May 2026, a larger event saw 41 public health technologies transferred to industry partners.

The National Medical Commission (NMC) in early July 2026 issued an advisory asking all medical colleges to use the Patent Mitra platform for patent filing and technology transfer, according to a Medical Buyer report, signalling growing institutional support for the initiative.

What's Next

Emcure and Biological E will now move the licensed technologies through further development, clinical evaluation, regulatory approvals, and manufacturing scale-up. For the Indian diaspora, particularly healthcare professionals and investors tracking India's pharmaceutical sector, the deals underscore the country's shift from generic drug manufacturing toward indigenous innovation. Both companies are established players in the domestic and global vaccine supply chain, positioning these technologies for potential international deployment once development milestones are met.
